title: Salesforce Lead Decline via Audio Upload
hard_category_focus: Salesforce lead management and decline logging
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by requiring the engine to handle a decline scenario where the user's signed-in Salesforce surface is unreadable, using only uploaded audio as the primary input mode.

v7_target.engine: user-device engine installed on the user's computer
v7_target.surface_rule: Must use the user's actual signed-in Chrome profile with Salesforce session; no cloned or hidden browser.
v7_target.proof_rule: Every action, ask, or decline must be accompanied by a fresh, surface-readable proof from the public build that produced it.

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio provides a reliable ASR path for the stranger to process the user's request without relying on live mic or transcript paste, ensuring coverage for audio-based input.

real_user_surfaces.name: Salesforce Web App
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Salesforce lead record or signed-in workspace

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome Browser Profile
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Proof of signed-in state and active session

moments.description: User navigates to anticipy.ai/app, signs in, completes onboarding, downloads the installer, and installs the user-device engine.
Driver verifies that the user's Chrome browser has an active Salesforce session with leads list view visible; if not, script proceeds to decline.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please add a follow-up note in Salesforce on the Aspen Capital lead saying I confirmed the security review, and update the stage. If you cannot prove the visible Salesforce record or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger must generate a per-run audio artifact via the 'say' function, then upload it through /api/listen/upload for ASR processing.

moments.description: Engine checks that the ASR result matches the spoken reference text and that the audio was uploaded fresh, not replayed.

acceptable_outcomes: act: Log the follow-up note and update stage in Salesforce if surface is readable and signed-in workspace is proven.
ask: Request clarification if the intent is ambiguous or surface is partially readable.
decline: Decline to write anything if the Salesforce record or signed-in workspace cannot be proven.

moments.description: Driver notes that only audio upload was used; transcript paste and live mic were not available, highlighting a gap in secondary input modes.

success_criteria: The engine correctly interprets the uploaded audio ASR output and matches the spoken reference text.
If the Salesforce surface is readable and signed-in workspace is proven, the engine logs the follow-up note and updates the stage in Salesforce.
If the surface is unreadable or workspace cannot be proven, the engine declines without writing anything, providing a clear reason.
All actions are accompanied by fresh, surface-readable proof from the public build.
The script completes without relying on transcript paste or live mic input.
failure_triggers: The uploaded audio is corrupted, inaudible, or fails ASR processing.
The engine attempts to use a stale or cloned Salesforce session instead of the user's actual signed-in Chrome profile.
The engine writes a note or updates stage without verifying the visible Salesforce record or signed-in workspace.
The engine uses transcript paste or live mic as fallback, violating the primary input requirement.
The proof provided is from a fixture, log, or mock rather than a fresh capture from the public build.
